newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila court halts auction of television network.
newsitem.headline: Manila court halts auction of television network.

text.p: The Philippine Supreme Court on Friday halted bidding for assets of local television network International Broadcasting Corp (IBC).
The assets of IBC, or Channel 13, were scheduled to be auctioned by the state-owned Presidential Commission on Good Government at 3 p.m. (0700 GMT).

The court, acting on a petition filed by former IBC president Jose Jalandon, said the temporary restraining order on the commission would protect other major stockholders who were affected when the television company was sequestered 10 years ago.
The commission is the agency in charge of tracking assets of late former president Ferdinand Marcos, who was deposed from 20 years of rule in a popular revolt in 1986.
Channel 13 was owned by a Marcos associate until the commission sequestered its shares.
The commission said it has qualified 19 firms out of the 41 interested bidders in the IBC privatisation.
The court gave the commission 10 days to file its comments on the restraining order.
